To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

0.9% of children treated with the von Rosen cast for suspected neonatal instability of hip had avascular necrosis and that the ossification of the head of the femur was slower in those with neonatal instability than in children with a stable hip.
early treatment with the von Rosens splint for NIH was safe with respect to AVN, and that the ossification of the hip was slower in children treated early for NIH than in children with stable hips.

the ossification of the ossific nuclei in the femoral head in children with NIH is significantly smaller than in untreated children at the age of 1 year, and that the risk of AVH in children treated early for neonatally dislocated hip with the von Rosen is low.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the treatment of neonatal instability of hip.
the development and evaluation of new methods for the early treatment of congenital dislocation of the hip.
the early detection of developmental dysplasias of the hip and the prevention of their sequelae.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

early treatment with the von Rosens splint for NIH in children with dislocated hips does not increase the risk for AVN of the hip, and the ossification of the hip is slower than in children with neonatly stable hips.
the use of the von Rosen splints for the treatment of DDH does not lead to AVN of the femoral heads.
there is no evidence of an association between early treatment of NIH with the von Rosen brace and AVN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the von Rosen splints can be used safely for treatment of neonatal instability.

early treatment with von Rosen splint is safe for the hip and the ossific nucleus of the hip is smaller in children with neonatality dislocated hip compared to untreated children with neonatal stability.
the von Rosen splints are a safe treatment for DDH, and that the ossification of the ossific center is slower in children treated with von Rosen splints.

early treatment with the von Rosens splint for neonatally unstable hips is safe regarding AVNs of the femoral heads.
